citation: George Glessner, photograph of an Illinois Central train approaching 18th Street, looking north along the tracks, c. 1888-1895. Reproduced in "George Glessner, photographer", Glessner House blog, January 2015.
author: George Glessner
repository: Glessner House (the museum's collection, as reproduced on its blog)
locator: The blog's 'IC train' image; the project's copy is kevinrhaas/chicago-images prairie-1904/files/st-ghm-george-glessner-ic-train-18th.jpg (record st-ghm-george-glessner-ic-train-18th).
rights_note: Permission requested from Glessner House Museum, 2026-10-02 (chicago-images rights-requests/ghm-george-glessner-2026-10.md). Read for what it shows; not shipped in the scene.
access_notes: Read from the owner's image store copy; the museum's original was not seen. The date is the blog's attribution to George Glessner's years with a camera (he was born 1871), not a dated print.
note: Spent by T-2478 for the 1904 lakefront: seven or more tracks side by side on a dark, fine ballast filled nearly to the ties' tops, the same dark ground trodden flat between the tracks, no lawn and no pale broken stone, a stone-curbed edge on the west side and the open lake to the east.
what_it_supplies: The look of the ballast and the ground between the tracks: dark cinders filled up round the ties
That the yard was several tracks wide at 18th Street a decade and more before 1904
what_it_does_not_supply: Track positions or count as of 1904 (the 1911 Sanborn sheets supply those)
Summer vegetation: the view is bare or winter
